title: fix(import): createMissingOptions keeps the unmatched option value through the engine's option check
body:
Fixes #22183
Clause-②: yes (the enforce route widens what the import write accepts; a retirement is a narrowing, and this declaration stays)

## Route: enforce

`ImportRequest.createMissingOptions` now does what its description says. On an import that sets it, a `select` / `radio` / `multiselect` cell that matches none of the field's options is stored as written. The engine's option check admits exactly the values that import kept, on that import's writes.

I took the enforce route from the triage direction (comment 6052894103). The measurements below show that it holds:

- a later edit that leaves the field out stays accepted;
- keeping the value needs no write to the field's option metadata.

So neither stop condition in the dispatch fired.

## Measurements (before the fix, this tree at `9f0de32a`)

| | Reading | How |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **H1** | Holds. With the flag on, coercion keeps `Priority = "Bogus"`, and the engine refuses it with `Priority must be one of: high, low`. The multiselect is refused with `Tags: "Bogus" is not one of: important, review`. The dry run does the same. A `readonly` select is dropped by the insert strip. On a historical update import it is stored shape-only. With the flag off, coercion refuses all three cells with `invalid_option`. | A throwaway probe (not committed): `runImport` through `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` over a real `ObjectQL`, flag on and off, dry run and write. |
| **H2** | Holds. No code path adds a kept value to the field's options. The repo grep finds only the coercion branch. The "create" reading of the key's name would need a data import to write object metadata (an overlay per field, with metadata write permission, on packaged objects too). The "keep" reading needs a typed signal on the write and an admission in the option arm. The spec describe and objectui's checkbox label (*Keep unknown option values*) both state the keep reading, so that is the one implemented. | `git grep createMissingOptions` (this repo, objectui `main`) |
| **H3** | **Frozen, not bricked.** The probe seeded a row holding `priority: "Bogus"`, `tags: ["Bogus", "important"]`. A partial update that leaves the field out is **accepted** (engine `update` and `DataProtocol.updateData`). An update that sends the field back unchanged is **refused** (`invalid_option`). So is a multiselect edit that keeps the off-list item, and so is a whole-record echo. Changing the value to an option is accepted. The option arm judges only the payload's keys (`validateRecordInScope`, update walk), never the stored row. objectui's edit form sends only the fields that changed (`dirtyEditPayload`, objectui#10156). | the same probe |
| **H4** | Holds. objectui's Import Wizard is the one sender of `true` (`assembleImportRequest`, the `import-opt-create-options` checkbox). In this repo, `connector-pull.ts` and `admin-import-users.ts` send `false`, and `import-prepare.ts` reads the body. | objectui at `f3a0488`. The one commit to `main` since touches none of these files. |

## The change

- **`@objectstack/spec`**
  - `ExecutionContext.keptOptionValues` (`Record<string, string[]>`) is a declared, server-constructed per-write key, next to `skipStateMachine` and `preserveAudit`, the flags the same import runner already sets. It holds, per field, the option values the import kept. It is never client-supplied.
  - The `ImportRequest.createMissingOptions` describe now says exactly what is enforced.
- **`@objectstack/core`**
  - `coerceFieldValue` reports the values it kept, and `coerceRow` returns them as `keptOptionValues`.
  - `runImport` puts exactly those values on each write's context:
    - a per-row `createData` / `updateData` and the dry run's `validateData` carry the row's own values;
    - a batched `createManyData` / `insertManyData` carries the union of its rows' values (one call carries one context).
  - A row that kept nothing is written with the import's context unchanged. With the option off, every write is byte-identical to before.
- **`@objectstack/objectql`**
  - `ValidateRecordOptions.keptOptionValues`: the single-value and multi-value option arms admit a listed value and still refuse every other value outside the options. The refusal still names the declared options, and a picklist that did not resolve stays refused.
  - The engine passes the write's `ExecutionContext.keptOptionValues` at its four writable-field validation calls: `validate`, insert, by-id update and predicate update. The two readonly-only `'only'` passes are untouched, because a readonly value never reaches the option constraint.

Not a `??` tolerance and not an untyped bag. The signal is a declared spec key with one producer and one reader, and the admission is per field and per value.

## Landing outside the claim's file surface, and why

- `packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts`: the typed signal has to be declared somewhere, and `ExecutionContext` is where its two import siblings live. The import write reaches the engine only as `{ data, context }` through the protocol, and the protocol request has no other server-only slot.
- `packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts` and its test: the compile-time closed field set forces every new `ExecutionContext` key to be classified. `keptOptionValues` is a per-write flag that no transport entry resolves.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`: the validator is reached only through these call sites, so passing the context's value needs four one-line changes there. No overlap with the open engine PRs named in the claim: their hunks sit near line 5725, this PR's near 12916 to 15428.
- Generated artifacts: `packages/spec/authorable-surface/kernel.json` (written by the spec build), and `content/docs/references/{api/export,data/data-engine,kernel/execution-context}.mdx` (`gen:docs`, the one artifact `check:generated` proved stale).

## Tests (cited at the final head `2917976c`, unless stated)

- New:
  - `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner-kept-options.test.ts` (6): every write path and the dry run carry exactly their rows' kept values; option off means no key.
  - `packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.kept-option-values.test.ts` (6): both arms, both modes, per-field scope, an unresolved picklist.
  - `packages/objectql/src/import-kept-option-values.test.ts` (7): the real engine end to end. Kept values are stored on the batched path, the per-row path, an update-mode import and the dry run. The option-off control. The admission is the import's only. A later edit leaves the field out (accepted), sends it back (refused) or picks an option (accepted).
  - One case in `packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.test.ts`.
- `@objectstack/core`, both projects: **82 files, 2247 tests passed**. `typecheck` exit 0 (test layer OK).
- `@objectstack/objectql` local project: **382 files, 7533 tests passed**. Repo project: 1 file, 5 tests passed. `typecheck` exit 0 (test layer OK, debt unchanged). The local run and the typecheck were taken at `4305775d`. `git diff 4305775d..2917976c` touches no file under `packages/objectql` or `packages/spec/src`, only the changeset, generated docs and one core test line.
- `@objectstack/spec`: `src/kernel` and `src/api` suites passed. `typecheck` exit 0 (at `4305775d`, same argument).

## Reverse verification (one-shot, both from committed state)

- **Engine admission ablated** (`keptOptionsFor` made to return nothing, in the `src` the suites import). Applied with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 to 0, blob `c30d7977` to `abef8f2f`. Result: **9 red / 4 green** across the two objectql files. The 4 green are the controls (per-field scope, unresolved picklist, option-off, plain write refused). Restored blob equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Runner hand-over ablated** (`writeCtxFor` made to return the import context unchanged), through core's `dist/`. Rebuild, then `ablation-dist-preflight` showed the marker present in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`. Result: objectql end-to-end **5 red / 2 green**, core runner pins **5 red / 1 green** (the option-off control). Restore leg: blob equals HEAD, rebuild, `--absent` reads the marker absent from all 14 built files, and the tree is clean.

## Gates (final head `2917976c`)

- `dispatch-gates --commands` re-derived after the change gives 116 families: the dispatch's 84, plus 32 that the diff reaches (engine-double, type-check-coverage/debt, docs families from the regenerated references, `check:generated`, …). **All 116 ran.**
  - 113 exited 0 on the first run.
  - 3 first answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET: two shallow-history gates and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, which needs a whole-repo build. They exited 0 once the clone was deepened (`--shallow-since=2026-07-03`) and the repo built (71/72 cache hits).
- Key readings: `check:authorable-surface`, `check:api-surface`, `check:liveness`, `check:generated` (all 15 up to date), `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:type-check-debt` and `check:nul-bytes` all exit 0.
- No `pnpm lint` run locally. The full lint is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **The H3 boundary, stated in the describe.** A later write that sends the field back unchanged is judged against the options and refused. Rows whose value left the option list some other way (an option removed from a field) are treated the same today. The option arm judges the payload, never the stored row. objectui's edit form sends only changed fields, with one exception: a save with nothing changed resends the whole loaded record (`dirtyEditPayload`), and that save is refused with the option sentence until the user picks an option. Not filed: it is the existing posture for any stored off-list value, and the stop condition in the dispatch put widening it out of this card. Carrier: none.
- **Import undo** (`rest-server.ts`, restore of `u.before` through `updateData`) cannot restore a prior value that is no longer in the options. It is counted `failed`. This was already true for option-removed values. It is now also reachable after a kept import followed by an update import. Not reproduced here. Carrier: none.
- **Batch union.** A batched create carries the union of its rows' kept values, because one call carries one context. A `beforeInsert` hook that writes one of those exact values onto another row of the same batch is therefore admitted. A hook value outside the union is refused.
- **objectui follow-up for the seat** (named by the card, not a new finding): `refusedOptionValue` in `packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx` (objectui#11886) still marks an unknown value on a writable field when *Keep unknown option values* is ticked. With this PR the server keeps it, so the preview should spare every option field when the box is ticked, and that docblock's sentence about the engine still refusing becomes false.
